details: A dull knife is slower, less precise, and more dangerous than a sharp one, the 3-Stage Knife Sharpener restores damaged, worn, and dull blades back to a clean, sharp edge — in three progressive steps that actually address the blade properly rather than just scraping the surface. Most basic sharpeners only do one thing — grind the edge down slightly and call it sharp. The three-stage system here works the blade progressively: the diamond-coated rod repairs and realigns damaged edges first, the tungsten steel stage refines and sharpens the edge properly, and the ceramic rod finishes with a polished, smooth edge that holds its sharpness longer between sessions. That sequence matters because skipping straight to a fine sharpener on a damaged blade produces a sharp but short-lived result. The non-slip base and ergonomic handle keep the unit stable and controlled throughout, which is important when drawing a blade through a sharpener repeatedly. Key Features Stage 1 — diamond-coated rod → Repairs and straightens visibly damaged or rolled edges before sharpening begins — essential for blades that have been neglected or used hard. Stage 2 — tungsten steel blades → Sharpens and rebuilds the edge with precision, restoring the cutting angle and strength of the blade after the repair stage. Stage 3 — ceramic rod → Polishes and refines the finished edge, leaving a smooth, clean surface that reduces drag during cutting and extends the time between sharpening sessions. Non-slip base → Keeps the sharpener firmly in place on the counter while drawing the blade through — critical for both safety and consistent sharpening angle. Ergonomic handle → Provides a secure, comfortable grip throughout the sharpening process, reducing hand fatigue when working through multiple knives. Compatible with a wide range of knife types → Works across chef's knives, utility knives, paring knives, and more — covers your full knife block in one tool. The difference between 31 blades and a basic mallet-style tenderizer is coverage and consistency — every press drives all 31 stainless steel blades through the meat simultaneously, breaking down fibres evenly across the surface rather than just pounding one area at a time.
